question.text: Which HTML tag defines the largest heading?
question.explain: Headings run from h1 (largest) to h6 (smallest). The head tag holds page metadata, not a heading.

question.text: Which element is meant for a block of main navigation links?
question.explain: The nav element is the semantic HTML5 container for major navigation links.

question.text: Which element holds self-contained content such as a blog post?
question.explain: An article is independent content that makes sense on its own, such as a post or news story.

question.text: Which CSS property changes the text colour?
question.explain: The color property sets text colour. background-color sets the background.
Flexbox lays items out along one axis (row or column) and distributes space between them.

question.text: Which unit is relative to the root element's font size?
question.explain: rem means "root em": it scales with the font size of the html element.

question.text: Which array method adds an item to the end?
question.explain: push() appends to the end. pop() removes from the end, and unshift() adds to the start.
This is a long-standing quirk of JavaScript: typeof null is "object".
Strict equality checks both value and type, with no type conversion.

question.text: A PHP variable name starts with which symbol?
question.explain: All PHP variables begin with a dollar sign, for example $name.

question.text: Which PHP function counts the elements of an array?
question.explain: count() returns the number of elements in an array.

question.text: Which superglobal holds data from a form that uses method="post"?
question.explain: $_POST contains values sent in the HTTP request body by a POST form.

question.text: Which technology defines the allowed structure of an XML document?
question.explain: A DTD (Document Type Definition) lists the elements and attributes a valid document may contain.
In XML, <Name> and <name> are different elements, and opening and closing tags must match exactly.

question.text: Which language transforms XML into HTML?
question.explain: XSLT applies template rules to an XML tree and produces HTML or other output.
